User:
Short description:
Duo multi-factor not working after replacing phone
Long description:
From: Okafor, Sam <sam_okafor@omu.example>
Sent: Tuesday, March 10, 2026 8:02 AM
Subject: New phone, Duo prompts not arriving

I upgraded my phone over the weekend and restored from a backup. Duo opens but it never receives a push, and the passcodes it generates are rejected. I cannot get into anything that needs two-factor.

Agent:
Restoring from a backup copies the Duo app but not the cryptographic keys it holds - those are tied to the old hardware and deliberately do not transfer. The app looks fine and generates codes, but they are codes for a device the server no longer recognises. The fix is to re-enrol the new phone rather than repair the old entry.

Agent:
I have sent a self-enrolment link to your OMU address; it is valid for 24 hours. Open it on a computer, not the phone, choose Add a Device, pick Duo Mobile, and scan the QR code with the app. Delete the restored account entry in Duo first or you will have two entries and no way to tell them apart.

User:
Done. Pushes arrive again. Should I do anything different next time I replace a phone?

Agent:
Yes - re-enrol the new phone before you wipe the old one, while you can still approve a push from the old device to authorise the change. That turns a support ticket into a two-minute self-service task. I have noted the new device on your account and I am closing this out.

Resolution:
To fix Duo after replacing a phone, re-enrol the new device. Restoring from a backup copies the Duo app but not the keys it holds, so the codes it produces are rejected. Delete the restored entry in Duo Mobile, open the self-enrolment link on a computer, choose Add a Device, pick Duo Mobile, and scan the QR code with the new phone. Where possible re-enrol the new phone before wiping the old one, so a push to the old device can authorise the change and no support ticket is needed.

My laptop will not stay on Olympus Secure. It connects for a minute, drops, and then asks for the password again in a loop. Olympus Guest works fine. This started after I changed my OMU password last week.

Agent:
That loop is the symptom of a stale saved network profile. Olympus Secure authenticates with your OMU credentials, so when you changed the password the stored profile kept presenting the old one, failed, and prompted you again.

Forgetting the network fixed it. It has held for the last two hours.

Good. Note the same thing will happen on your phone if it also has Olympus Secure saved, so forget and rejoin it there too the next time you rotate your password. Resolving the ticket.

Resolution:
To fix a wireless connection that repeatedly asks for the password, forget and rejoin the network. Olympus Secure authenticates with OMU credentials, so after a password change the saved profile keeps offering the old one and the prompt loops. On macOS use System Settings, Wi-Fi, Details, Forget This Network; on Windows use Settings, Network and Internet, Wi-Fi, Manage known networks, Forget. Reconnect, enter the new password once and accept the certificate. Repeat on every device that has the network saved, phones included.

User:
Short description:
Jobs failing on Caldera with disk quota exceeded
Long description:
From: Nakamura, Yuki <yuki_nakamura@omu.example>
Sent: Wednesday, June 17, 2026 4:48 PM
Subject: Caldera jobs dying, quota error

All of my Caldera jobs died overnight with "Disk quota exceeded". I have not changed anything about the pipeline. How do I find what is using the space?

Agent:
Run "quota -s" on a login node to see where you stand. Home directories are capped at 100 GB and that cap is on the directory, not on any one file, so a single run that writes intermediates into your home will exhaust it.

Almost always the cause is job output written to home rather than to scratch. Check for slurm-*.out files in your home directory - a job array that logs there can produce tens of thousands of them.

User:
There were about 40,000 slurm out files. Deleted them and I am back to 20 percent used.

Agent:
That will keep happening unless the pipeline stops writing there. Two changes are worth making now.

Point job output at scratch with an sbatch directive of the form --output=/caldera/scratch/<your id>/logs/%j.out, and write intermediates to scratch as well. Scratch gives you 25 TB but it is purged after 45 days without access, so treat anything there as disposable and copy finished results back to lab storage.

Agent:
For results you need to keep beyond 45 days, request lab storage on the Vault tier rather than growing the home quota - the home cap is not raised for this reason. Closing as resolved.

Resolution:
To clear a "Disk quota exceeded" failure on Caldera, run "quota -s" on a login node to see usage, then delete the job logs filling the home directory. Home is capped at 100 GB and a job array logging there can leave tens of thousands of slurm-*.out files. Stop it recurring by sending job output to scratch with an sbatch directive such as --output=/caldera/scratch/<your id>/logs/%j.out and writing intermediates there too. Scratch holds 25 TB but is purged after 45 days without access, so copy finished results back. For anything that must outlive 45 days, request lab storage on the Vault tier rather than asking for a larger home quota.

Mailbox full, cannot send or receive
Long description:
From: Whitfield, Tom <tom_whitfield@omu.example>
Sent: Friday, July 3, 2026 10:05 AM
Subject: Mailbox is full

Outlook says my mailbox is full and I cannot send anything. I have deleted a lot of mail but nothing has changed.

Agent:
Deleted mail still counts against the quota until it leaves Deleted Items, and Deleted Items itself is retained for 30 days. That is why the number has not moved. Empty Deleted Items, then empty Recoverable Items via the Recover Deleted Items dialog in Outlook for Web.

The mailbox limit is 50 GB. To see what is actually consuming it, use the Mailbox Storage view in Outlook for Web settings, which breaks usage down by folder.

User:
Recoverable Items had 12 GB in it. That did it. Anything I should do so this does not recur?

Agent:
Large attachments are what fills a mailbox, so stop mailing files around. Put them on OneDrive or the lab share and send the link instead - it does not count against your quota, the recipient always gets the current version, and there is no size ceiling to work around.

Sorting by size in Outlook and clearing the largest twenty messages once a term keeps you comfortably under the limit. Marking this resolved.

Resolution:
To fix a full mailbox, empty Deleted Items and then empty Recoverable Items through the Recover Deleted Items dialog in Outlook for Web. Deleted mail counts against the 50 GB quota until it leaves both, which is why deleting alone frees nothing. Use the Mailbox Storage view in Outlook for Web settings to see which folders are consuming space. To stop it recurring, stop mailing attachments: put files on cloud storage or the lab share and send a link, which does not count against the quota and has no size ceiling.

Do not keep power cycling it - a repeated interrupted boot is how a recoverable filesystem problem becomes an unrecoverable one. Bring it to Deskside Support and we will look at it today given the Thursday deadline.

If you need the slides sooner than the repair, we can pull the drive contents in about an hour with a target disk boot, provided you know your FileVault password. The encryption key is escrowed with us, so the data is recoverable either way.

Diagnostics point at a failing internal SSD - the SMART counters show reallocated sectors climbing. The machine is 14 months old so it is inside the three-year AppleCare term and the replacement is covered.

We recovered your full home directory to a loaner before sending the unit out, and the loaner has your account, your slides and the standard software set on it. Turnaround from Apple is three to five business days.

Loaner is working and I have the slides. Thank you for the quick turnaround.

Repaired unit is back, restored from the recovery image, and swapped for the loaner. One thing worth saying: the recovery worked because the drive was still partly readable, which is luck rather than a plan. Turn on Time Machine to the lab NAS, or keep working files in OneDrive, so the next failure costs you nothing. Closing.

Resolution:
To handle a laptop that will not boot past the vendor logo, stop power cycling it and bring it to Deskside Support: a repeatedly interrupted boot turns a recoverable filesystem problem into an unrecoverable one. Data can usually be pulled in about an hour with a target disk boot, and the encryption key is escrowed with Deskside Support so it is recoverable either way. A failing SSD inside the warranty term is replaced at no cost, with a loaner issued carrying the user's account and files. User:
Short description:
Department printer not accepting jobs
Long description:
From: Reyes, Jordan <jordan_reyes@omu.example>
Sent: Wednesday, December 3, 2026 2:40 PM
Subject: Printer on 4th floor queues but never prints

Jobs sit in the queue on the fourth floor printer and never come out. Other people say the same. The panel on the device shows no error.

Agent:
When a shared queue accepts jobs and nothing prints, it is nearly always the print server holding them rather than the device. I have cleared the stuck queue - one malformed job was blocking everything behind it.

Try again and let me know. If it recurs, note which application the job came from; a badly generated PDF is the usual culprit.

User:
It printed. It was a PDF from a scanner that jammed the queue before.

Agent:
That matches. Those scanner PDFs are non-standard and the printer's interpreter stalls on them rather than rejecting them, which is what blocks the whole queue.

Open them in a PDF reader and re-export or print as image before sending, and they will go through. I have also enabled a job timeout on that queue so one bad job drops after five minutes instead of blocking indefinitely. Resolving.

Resolution:
To fix a shared printer that queues jobs but never prints, clear the stuck queue on the print server: one malformed job blocks everything behind it, and the device itself reports no error because the fault is not on the device. Scanner-produced PDFs are the usual culprit, as the printer's interpreter stalls on them rather than rejecting them. Open such a file in a PDF reader and re-export it, or print as image, before sending. Setting a job timeout on the queue makes a bad job drop after five minutes instead of blocking indefinitely.

User:
Short description:
Cannot set up OMU email on personal phone
Long description:
From: Haddad, Leila <leila_haddad@omu.example>
Sent: Friday, January 16, 2026 4:10 PM
Subject: Phone will not accept my email password

I am trying to add my OMU email to my phone. It takes the address, asks for the password, and then says the credentials are wrong. The same password works fine in a browser.

Agent:
The built-in mail app on both iOS and Android uses a legacy protocol that we disabled, so it fails even with the correct password. That is the difference between it and the browser.

Install Microsoft Outlook from the app store and add the account there. It uses modern authentication, so it will hand you to the normal sign-in page and prompt you for Duo, and it will work.

User:
Outlook worked straight away. Is there a reason the normal mail app is blocked?

Agent:
The legacy protocol cannot carry a second factor, so an account reachable through it is protected by a password alone - which is exactly what credential-stuffing attacks are looking for. Disabling it closes that path across the whole institution.

The other reason to use Outlook on a personal phone is that we can remove the OMU account remotely if the phone is lost, without touching anything else on it. Closing as resolved.

Resolution:
To set up OMU email on a personal phone, install Microsoft Outlook from the app store and add the account there. The built-in mail app on iOS and Android uses a legacy protocol that is disabled, so it rejects a correct password while the same password works in a browser. The legacy protocol cannot carry a second factor, which leaves an account protected by a password alone and is exactly what credential-stuffing attacks look for, so it is disabled institution-wide. Outlook also allows the OMU account to be removed remotely if the phone is lost, without touching anything else on it.

User:
Short description:
R package installation failing on Caldera
Long description:
From: Ibrahim, Nadia <nadia_ibrahim@omu.example>
Sent: Tuesday, February 24, 2026 11:22 AM
Subject: install.packages fails on Caldera

install.packages fails on Caldera with a permission denied error. I assume I cannot write to the system library. Can you install the packages for me?

Agent:
We do not install R packages centrally, because pinning one version institution-wide breaks somebody else's pipeline every time it moves. You install into a personal library instead, which you can do without any help from us.

Load a module first with "module load gcc/9.2.0 R/4.3.1", then in R run install.packages with a lib argument pointing at a directory you own, such as ~/R/4.3.1/library. Create it first. Set R_LIBS_USER in your ~/.Rprofile so the path is picked up automatically afterwards.

User:
That worked for most packages but the ones needing compilation still fail on the login node.

Agent:
Compilation on a login node is capped on memory and CPU on purpose - it is a shared shell host, not a build machine. Compiling anything substantial there either fails or gets killed.

Request an interactive session first with "srun --pty -t 2:00:00 -p interactive --mem 8G bash", then install from inside it. Eight gigabytes is enough for most source packages.

User:
All installed from the interactive session. Thank you.

Agent:
Worth knowing for later: keep a separate library directory per R version, because packages built against one R do not load under another and mixing them produces errors that look like corrupt installs. Closing.

Resolution:
To install R packages on Caldera, install into a personal library rather than the system one. Load a module with "module load gcc/9.2.0 R/4.3.1", create a directory you own such as ~/R/4.3.1/library, and pass it to install.packages as the lib argument; set R_LIBS_USER in ~/.Rprofile so the path is picked up automatically thereafter. Packages needing compilation must be built inside an interactive session rather than on a login node, which is memory- and CPU-capped: request one with "srun --pty -t 2:00:00 -p interactive --mem 8G bash". Keep a separate library directory per R version, because packages built against one R do not load under another.

User:
Short description:
Guidance on using AI tools with research data
Long description:
From: Park, Helen <helen_park@omu.example>
Sent: Monday, March 30, 2026 10:45 AM
Subject: Can we use AI tools on our data?

Our group wants to use a large language model to help summarise clinical notes for a study. What is allowed and what tooling should we use?

Agent:
The dividing line is where the data goes, not which model you use. A public consumer service sends the data to a third party and may retain it for training, so it is not permitted for anything containing PHI or other sensitive research data regardless of what the study protocol says.

The AI Sandbox is the supported route. It runs under a OMU agreement with no training on submitted content and no retention beyond the session, and it is approved for internal and confidential data.

User:
The notes contain PHI. Does the Sandbox cover that?

Agent:
Not on its own. PHI needs a documented IRB protocol covering the AI processing and a review from the security office, and it has to run in the high-security tier of the Sandbox rather than the standard one.

Bring the protocol number to the security office review and they will confirm the tier and any additional controls. Expect two to three weeks for that.

Agent:
One practical note for the meantime: de-identifying the notes before they reach any model removes most of this burden and is usually feasible for summarisation work. If the study design allows it, that is much the faster path. I am leaving the ticket open pending the security review.

Resolution:
Guidance on using AI tools with research data: what matters is where the data goes, not which model is used. Public consumer services send data to a third party and may retain it for training, so they are not permitted for PHI or other sensitive research data whatever the study protocol says. The OMU AI Sandbox is the supported route, running under an institutional agreement with no training on submitted content and no retention beyond the session, approved for internal and confidential data. PHI additionally needs a documented IRB protocol covering the AI processing, a security office review, and the high-security tier of the Sandbox; allow two to three weeks. De-identifying records before they reach any model removes most of this burden and is usually the faster path for summarisation work.
